title: From Intervention Point to Implementation
description: Sequence five design steps from choosing an intervention point to closing the feedback loop, with a hospital-scheduling example at each step.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Systems Design, Emerging Technology, and Practice
chapter_title: Systems Design, Emerging Technology, and Practice

educational.learningObjective: Given a proposed system change, the learner will sequence the design steps from choosing an intervention point through closing the feedback loop, and explain what each step is meant to catch that the previous step could miss.
prerequisites: Knows what a leverage point is
Has proposed or observed an organizational change
learningOutcomes: Sequence the five design steps correctly
Explain what each step catches that the previous one misses
Describe why the workflow loops rather than terminates
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Give learners a proposed change and ask them to write one sentence per step, ending with what the flourishing check would look for.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Click-to-explain linear workflow with a closing loop
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Each step justified by what the previous step fails to catch
pedagogical.feedbackType: A definition plus a worked example applied to the same running scenario
misconceptionsAddressed: That implementation is the last step of a design process
That improving the target metric means the intervention worked
discussionQuestions: Why is the last step separate from the feedback mechanism in step 3?
What would it take for an organization to actually revise after the data surprised them?
Which of the five steps gets skipped most often, and what does skipping it cost?
